objective: Prove that a class-3 edge satisfying every clean-edge condition of Theorem 5 (COPRIME-PAIRS-20261027-001E) except the vertex-root condition (V3), whose dual slot carries no layer-1 data, makes counting #P-hard: the vertex equations are a conserved flow (COPRIME-PAIRS-20261027-001F, sections 1-2), the flow and the dual slot's constraints are linear in the dual slot's data, so the Fourier dual of every edge weight is a non-negative count, and the Brunnian rank witness applies. No off-diagonal vanishing or diagonal bilinearity is needed. Count the census algebras decided, with a control where the dual slot has layer-1 data.
status: Proved: a class-3 edge failing only the vertex-root condition, whose dual slot has no layer-1 data, makes counting #P-hard (Theorem 8: conserved flows linear in the dual slot's data have a non-negative Fourier dual); 8 new census algebras, the whole vertex-root family decided, 105 of 850 open.
title: Linear flows: class-3 vertex-root pair failures are #P-hard when the dual slot has no layer-1 data
